title: IKEMaker Tools
purpose: Find tools by the work you want to do.
firstAction: Expand Quick Start, Create New, or an authoring section.
source: The sidebar opens existing workspaces and commands.
safety: Opening a tool does not apply an edit.

title: Create an individual file
purpose: Start an asset or source file without needing an existing character.
firstAction: Choose a file type, then Browse to its destination.
source: The new file becomes the editable source.
safety: Review the destination and template before creation.

title: Character workbench
purpose: Open a character and its connected assets together.
firstAction: Browse to the character DEF and choose the workspaces you need.
source: DEF assignments connect code, AIR, SFF, and SND.
safety: Check the character and game context before editing.

title: Artist Intake and temporary SFF
purpose: Turn artist frames into a temporary sprite archive while preserving source names and originals.
firstAction: Open a GIF, sprite sheet, or PNG frame folder. Select frames, enter a sequence name, group, image index and axes, then Assign selection. Scroll down to assignments in a narrow window.
source: Create Temporary SFF Package offers CS working SFF with one reviewed indexed PNG or 256-color ACT shared by every sprite, or General intake for intentionally different source palettes. Choose the destination and name, then Build temporary SFF in the notification.
safety: No AIR is created or changed. Invalid shared palettes and cancelled prompts create no package files. Review the built archive before use. Keep manifests and build evidence internal; share only the approved temporary SFF unless additional exports are requested.

title: SFF sprites and axes
purpose: Browse sprite groups and inspect their images and axes.
firstAction: Choose a group and sprite. Use Fit if the saved zoom clips the image; scroll down for the inspector in a narrow window.
source: The SFF owns images, palettes, and axes. More > Compare pins a frozen reference and compares another selected item. See Connected viewers, layouts, and comparison in Offline Docs for capture details, layout controls, and session limits.
safety: Preview changes before saving; keep archive backups enabled.

title: SFF palettes
purpose: Inspect embedded colors and the sprites that use each palette.
firstAction: Open Palettes in the inspector, then choose a palette.
source: Palette ownership stays attached to the archive and applicable sprites.
safety: Preview the affected sprites before saving color changes.
audience: Creator; Player palette replacement uses the roster flow

title: Sprite review notes
purpose: Track approval, axis checks, naming, and layer review.
firstAction: Open Review and select the sprite you are reviewing.
source: Review notes live in project metadata beside the asset.
safety: Saving a review note does not rewrite sprite pixels.

title: Sprite display and onion skin
purpose: Compare sprites with grids, axes, and an onion-skin reference.
firstAction: Open Display and choose the comparison options.
source: Display options change the preview.
safety: Panning the view does not move stored sprite axes.

title: Sprite layer preview
purpose: Inspect matching layers and their draw order.
firstAction: Open Layer Preview and enable a matching layer bank.
source: Layer numbering follows the selected project conventions.
safety: Review the composite before importing or rebuilding layers.

title: Sprite animation references
purpose: See which animations use the selected sprite.
firstAction: Open Animations and select a frame in the strip.
source: References come from connected AIR files. Use Open AIR for the assigned animation viewer. In AIR source, right-click a frame and choose Open Referenced Animation / FX / Sound / Sprite to select its SFF sprite.
safety: Selecting a frame changes the preview, not the AIR source.

title: AIR frames and playback
purpose: Review animation timing beside editable AIR code.
firstAction: Select an action and frame; press Play when you want motion.
source: Use Customize to show, hide, or reorder shared toolbar commands. Save remembers the layout for this viewer type; Reset restores defaults after Save. Cancel or Escape discards pending layout changes. More lists all shared commands, including hidden ones. Select an item and choose Used By to open searchable source references in a separate panel. Its line buttons open source; Refresh reads current unsaved text. Dynamic or ambiguous references are reported separately. Back and Forward follow source/viewer handoffs in this session; from a text editor use IKEMaker: Viewer History Back or Forward in the command palette. More > Compare pins a frozen reference and compares another selected item. See Connected viewers, layouts, and comparison in Offline Docs for capture details, layout controls, and session limits.
safety: Playback starts stopped; preview before applying edits.

title: AIR collision boxes
purpose: Inspect and edit attack and hurt boxes.
firstAction: Open Collision, select a visible box, and review its scope.
source: Clsn1 and Clsn2 edits belong to AIR.
safety: Check element versus default scope before Apply to AIR. Edits support VS Code Undo; your Auto Save setting still applies.

title: Push-box bridge
purpose: Inspect native character size alongside an animation.
firstAction: Open Push, enable Show push box, and choose the baseline pose or frame override.
source: Native Size and generated controllers remain code-owned.
safety: Push-box plans are not stored as invented AIR collision data.

title: Runtime geometry
purpose: Plan guard distance and transformed collision geometry.
firstAction: Open Runtime and choose the native field to inspect.
source: Copy native code into the appropriate character state.
safety: A saved preview plan does not prove in-game behavior; test it.

title: Animation source links
purpose: Find code associated with the current animation.
firstAction: Use Animation AIR Text in the toolbar to open a separate scrollable window that follows the selected action.
source: Open AIR Text Editor jumps to the selected action without opening automatically. The Open SFF button beside Pal FX selects the current frame sprite. The shared Open SFF and Open SND shortcuts open connected assets. Shared FX and sound references use configured CommonFX files, sound profiles, and motif FightFX. The shared prefix and archive appear above the toolbar; hover for the path and owner. This context survives a window reload and is checked against current configuration. If it says Shared context needs review, open a source reference to choose its context again. Duplicate prefixes ask you to choose the archive. Back to Source returns to the originating code line after reference navigation; if that line changes ambiguously, it asks you to reopen the reference.
safety: Explicit and inferred relationships remain distinguishable.

title: Collision rules
purpose: Explore native collision queries and interaction rules.
firstAction: Open Rules and select the feature you need.
source: Generated queries and HitDef rules belong in character code.
safety: Review copied code before applying it.

title: Animation layer preview
purpose: Review layered animation composition.
firstAction: Open Layers and enable the matching layer banks.
source: The preview follows the connected SFF and AIR.
safety: Layer preview does not rebuild either archive.

title: SND sounds
purpose: Browse sounds, view waveforms, and manage sound events.
firstAction: Select a group and sound; use Stop, Loop, and Volume to audition.
source: SND, sound profiles, and build manifests have separate roles. Right-click a PlaySnd reference in code and choose Open Referenced Animation / FX / Sound / Sprite to select that sound. Shared prefixes require choosing the correct archive when ambiguous. More > Compare pins a frozen reference and compares another selected item. See Connected viewers, layouts, and comparison in Offline Docs for capture details, layout controls, and session limits.
safety: Structural edits use a reviewed build workspace and backups.

title: Move Lab
purpose: Move between attack, throw, animation, and testing tools.
firstAction: Confirm the character, then choose a mode across the top. In a narrow editor, scroll below the preview to reach specialist tools, connected files, and diagnostics.
source: Connected files and diagnostics link back to source code.
safety: Use preview and validation before applying specialist edits.

title: HitDef authoring
purpose: Review attack properties with a shared visual preview.
firstAction: From Move Lab, choose a connected source file. When opening from code, place the cursor in the attack controller first and confirm Character supplies the intended preview. In a narrow editor, scroll below the preview to reach the controller fields and generated code.
source: The selected CNS or ZSS controller remains authoritative.
safety: Review generated changes before applying them. Checked options are written; unchecking an existing option removes that line when you apply. VS Code Undo reverses the edit, and your Auto Save setting still applies. If the source has changed, use Follow Cursor to refresh before applying.

title: Move Lab — Constants integration
purpose: Review an optional constants-based move profile alongside animations as one Move Lab integration. Pinned Sources in the shared toolbar keeps chosen constants, common code, and functions in a separate tabbed preview. Hide it with Customize or find it in More. The preview follows direct text matches for the selected profile when Follow selected move is enabled; turn it off to keep inspecting another source. Source line buttons open the text editor with navigation history. Unsaved text updates the preview automatically.
firstAction: Choose the character and move you want to inspect.
source: Uses the selected character’s configured conventions.
safety: Review the preview and affected constants before saving.

title: Helper Lab
purpose: Inspect helper relationships and author helper behavior.
firstAction: Select a helper or recipe and review its tree and properties.
source: Helper definitions and maps remain in connected source.
safety: Validate the plan before inserting or updating a controller. Edits support VS Code Undo; your Auto Save setting still applies.

title: Throw Creator
purpose: Coordinate attacker and target timing, binds, and reactions.
firstAction: Choose a throw plan and inspect both timelines. In a narrow window, scroll below the preview to reach the plan and interaction controls.
source: Reviewed code and the saved throw plan stay connected.
safety: Preview both fighters and validate before applying.

title: Spatial Composer
purpose: Position Explod effects, fighters, and camera-related elements.
firstAction: Choose Explod Composer or Position & Camera and inspect the coordinate space. Drag to adjust the marker; Shift-drag pans and the wheel zooms. In a narrow editor, scroll below the preview and fields to reach generated code.
source: Explod and position plans generate native character code.
safety: Review the selected insertion source and generated code. Open insertion source, place the cursor on a blank line between controllers in the intended state or function, then return and choose Recheck context. Confirm the detected state/function or conditional block before Insert at cursor. Insertion rejects controller parameter blocks; Copy code remains available. VS Code Undo removes the insertion. Your VS Code Auto Save setting still applies. Center screen is available for screen placement; Snap to floor is available for world or relative placement.

title: Code Structure
purpose: Navigate states and controllers beside their source.
firstAction: Open a code file and select a state or controller to open its source line.
source: Source links reuse existing tabs. Viewer History Back can reopen the recorded block; More keeps hidden toolbar commands available.
safety: Navigation does not rewrite code. Changed or ambiguous block matches stop the history jump.

title: Controller authoring
purpose: Find native controllers and their options.
firstAction: Filter the controller list, then open documentation or insertion options.
source: Insertion targets the active source editor.
safety: Verify the active file and cursor before inserting code.

title: Command editor
purpose: Review input motions, timing, and movelist text.
firstAction: Choose the command or motion you want to inspect.
source: The configured command file and movelist remain authoritative.
safety: Review timing and source changes before saving.

title: Stage workspace and Stage Rig
purpose: Inspect stage layers, parallax, bounds, and camera settings.
firstAction: Browse to a stage DEF, select a background, and use the camera controls to inspect the preview. In a narrow editor, scroll below the preview and background list to reach the inspector.
source: Stage DEF, SFF, and optional interaction code stay linked.
safety: Position fields preview changes until Apply reviewed position is confirmed. Recovery Center can restore the saved backup. Stage Rig uses the game's configured button mappings; its generated character is for development only.

title: Screenpack and fight UI
purpose: Screenpack and Fight UI reconstruct the 2D motif layout from its DEF, SFF, AIR, font references, and editor-only sample data.
firstAction: Browse to a motif or fight DEF, choose a section, then select an element. Menu entries inherit their parent menu anchor and use representative labels when runtime text is unavailable. In a narrow editor, scroll below the preview and element list to reach position fields.
source: DEF assets and optional Lua modules keep their own responsibilities.
safety: Bitmap FNT v2 default-bank ASCII glyphs are supported. Unsupported legacy fonts, other banks, or dynamic engine/Lua content use an approximate placeholder at the inherited position. Launch IKEMEN for the authoritative final rendering. Position changes write only after Apply reviewed position is confirmed.

title: Roster Manager
purpose: Arrange characters, orders, stages, and player options.
firstAction: Browse to select.def and choose the area you want to change.
source: Roster changes stay synchronized with select.def.
safety: Use safe mode and review changes before applying. Edits support VS Code Undo; your Auto Save setting still applies.

title: Story and dialogue
purpose: Build ordered scenes, dialogue, and choices.
firstAction: Choose a story or add a scene and inspect its preview.
source: Story data connects to native game launch and dialogue behavior.
safety: Review the route before applying and launching it.

title: Storyboard editor
purpose: Build opening, ending, credits, and other storyboard sequences. The preview shows layer positions and references; check rendered sprites, fonts, animation, and timing in the game.
firstAction: Browse to a storyboard DEF and select a scene. Set its duration in whole ticks and its clear color as three RGB values from 0 to 255, then choose Apply scene changes. Use + Scene, Duplicate, or the layer button to extend the sequence.
source: Open source jumps to the selected scene in the DEF for detailed fades, music, and layer timing. After saving source changes, use Refresh. Reopening the same storyboard reuses its editor tab.
safety: Scene changes write to the DEF with recovery history. If the file changes outside this editor, the edit is rejected: save or undo any unsaved source edits, choose Refresh, and review the scene before trying again. Use the Recovery Center to restore a prior saved version.

title: Menu and modes
purpose: Configure player-facing menu and mode recipes.
firstAction: Choose a mode and inspect its options.
source: Menu maps and native launch settings remain connected.
safety: Preview the recipe before applying changes. Edits support VS Code Undo; your Auto Save setting still applies.

title: Project and Team Manager
purpose: Organize games, projects, teams, and tracked work.
firstAction: Select the game and project before editing its team or tickets.
source: One game assignment identifies each project’s ownership.
safety: Review the selected project before attaching or changing records.

title: Production Workflow
purpose: Track project issues, tester feedback, authoring milestones, and review evidence.
firstAction: Choose the character, then Project Tickets or Report Intake. Expand Log a project issue or feedback. Add a title, what happened, and what you would have liked to happen; use-case notes and evidence references are optional.
source: IKEMaker version is recorded automatically. Expand Context and reproduction details to check item type/name/content version, profile and screen, or read declared name/version from a DEF. Unknown and manual entry are supported. Reviewed tickets retain this context.
safety: Check the named project and destination before saving. Title and what happened are required. Evidence paths and links are references; include the files when sharing. Changing item type resets unrelated name/version defaults.

title: Test and Diagnostic Suite
purpose: Prepare repeatable test sessions and inspect findings.
firstAction: Choose a test type and confirm the active character and game.
source: Tests connect to source diagnostics and runtime evidence.
safety: Use disposable copies for tests that change files.

title: Recovery Center
purpose: Inspect recorded edits and recover a saved backup.
firstAction: Open Recovery Center from the asset you want to restore, or Browse for its .ikemen-tools/mutations.json history. Select a recorded change and inspect its backup.
source: History points to the actual files and backup records.
safety: Review the restore target before recovering.

title: Complete Project
purpose: Prepare a reviewed public copy of a game.
firstAction: Use a disposable rehearsal and inspect the release profile first.
source: Release defaults, manifests, and checksums describe the output.
safety: Keep the development copy; verify the exported copy before sharing.

title: Learning and Advanced presentation
purpose: Choose how much guidance appears around the tools.
firstAction: Select the workspace presentation you prefer.
source: Presentation changes retain the same authoring capability.
safety: Conventions remain configurable per project.

title: Settings and launch configuration
purpose: Configure file exceptions, safety options, workflow preferences, and the shared destination-color presentation.
firstAction: Search the extension settings for the option you need. Set IKEMaker: Destination Colors to Off when you prefer neutral navigation controls.
source: Settings can be scoped to the current workspace. Destination Colors changes presentation only; labels, tooltips, focus, routing, and files remain unchanged.
safety: Check scope before changing a preference. Turning destination colors off does not disable or reroute any tool.

title: Help and Learning
purpose: Find a screen, understand its purpose, and open its tool.
firstAction: Search the Screen Guide or choose an offline document.
source: The guide links to installed tools and bundled documentation.
safety: Screenshots illustrate the tool; verify your own active context.
